stem.text: Let g be a continuous function with \( \int_{1}^{4} g(x)\,dx = -3 \) and \( \int_{7}^{4} g(x)\,dx = 5 \). Find the value of \( \int_{7}^{1} \left(2g(x) + 2\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Join the adjacent intervals: \( \int_{1}^{7} g(x)\,dx = \int_{1}^{4} g(x)\,dx + \int_{4}^{7} g(x)\,dx = -3 + (-5) = -8 \), since reversing \( \int_{7}^{4} \) changes its sign.
Reverse the requested integral: \( \int_{7}^{1} \left(2g(x) + 2\right) dx = -(2) \int_{1}^{7} g(x)\,dx + (2)(1 - 7) \), and the constant contributes \( -12 \).

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, both a supplied integral and the requested one run right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: constant multiple plus a constant term

distractor_derivations.A: sign change for the reversed target integral left out
distractor_derivations.B: given integral from 7 to 4 used as if it ran from 4 to 7
distractor_derivations.D: constant term integrated as if its limits ran left to right, so its sign change is left out
